Overall quality: **6/10**. The project is small, readable, and the documented fixture path is covered well: `pytest -q` passes with **58 tests**. I would **not approve as-is**, mainly because malformed inputs can crash ingest, XML handling is not hardened, and re-ingesting changed data leaves stale rows in the database.

Estimated rewrite/significant-change size: **about 260 LOC**, mostly parser hardening/streaming, ingest replacement semantics, and tests for malformed inputs.

issues.description: Re-ingesting changed inputs only upserts new rows and leaves stale results from prior ingests.
Format B assumes metrics is a dict; malformed JSON objects can crash ingest with AttributeError.
Malformed Format C XML raises ParseError and crashes instead of producing a structured warning.
XML parsing uses stdlib ElementTree without defusedxml or size/depth limits for untrusted input.
CSV and JSONL files are fully read into memory instead of streamed, risking memory blowups on large eval outputs.
Format A parses CSV one physical line at a time, so valid quoted multiline CSV fields are mishandled.
Required identifiers and dimensions can be empty or missing, creating low-quality records and possible overwrite collisions.
Model aliases accumulate across ingest passes and are never reconciled with the latest input set.
Empty input directories still create or mutate the database before the CLI returns an error.
Package metadata is minimal and lacks readme/license/authors and test/development dependency declarations.
Tests cover generated happy-path quirks but miss malformed JSON/XML, stale re-ingest behavior, and large-file streaming cases.
